newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro Group asks for emergency loans.
newsitem.headline: Jinro Group asks for emergency loans.

text.p: South Korea's Jinro Group has asked for 500 billion won in emergency loans from the Commercial Bank of Korea and SEOULBANK, a group spokesman said on Thursday.
"We urgently need the money to pay back our debts," said Jinro spokesman Chun Young-taek.

Jinro, South Korea's 19th largest conglomerate, said on Monday it would sell off business lines and other assets because of financial pressures. The group said it would generate 1.2 trillion won by the end of 1998.
Chun denied local reports that the sale of idle lands in Seoul to a Hong Kong company, "Jesmond Korea," was part of its restructuring plan.
He said Jinro sold the real estate for 145.6 billion won last December after abandoning plans to build a hotel.
"We are expecting a committee established by financial institutions will come up with some steps to finance Jinro on Monday," he said.

The committee, which will include local banks, merchant banking corporations, securities houses and life insurers, will screen financially troubled companies and decide whether they will extend fresh loans. It will begin work from next Monday.

Jinro has scheduled a meeting for possible buyers on Friday to give details of sales plans. About 300 people are expected to participate, including top conglomerates such as Hyundai, Samsung and LG Groups -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
